arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Whisman argued that a judge deciding facts that raise a sentence violates the Sixth Amendment.
Mr. Link argued that the error in this case could not be subjected to harmless error analysis.
Ms. Millett argued that failure to submit an element to a jury is subject to harmless error analysis.
Mr. Whisman distinguished his case by noting the defendant was never put on notice of aggravated murder.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial. It asks if a judge can decide facts that raise a sentence above the standard range. the side that brought the case argues this violates constitutional rights. the opposing side argues the error was harmless.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between judge and jury powers in sentencing. It determines who decides facts that raise criminal penalties. The outcome shapes the core of the jury trial right in criminal law.
